limitations: Neither participant is independent of the final artifact as a whole.

Independence applies only to the opposite participant's listed change scope. Review-edge scopes are the journal's canonical work units and participant summaries are checked against them, but scope labels and author/reviewer assignments remain attestations rather than mechanically derived facts.
The schema-v2 journal and validator were implemented by Codex in response to Claude's finding; their structure is test-covered but the review infrastructure itself has no third-party reviewer.

findings.issue: The archive-derived prose claimed that USDT/KRX had never existed in legacy and that fallback always left three bank rows. The pinned code proves only the current allowlist, while iOS visibility can leave fewer than three rows and investing is not a bank.
findings.disposition: Scoped the claim to the pinned legacy source set and replaced the fixed row count with the actual investing/kb/hana overlap subject to user visibility. The frozen archive remains unchanged as provenance, not as a truth source.

findings.issue: The document promoted an uncommitted project.pbxproj observation to a current canonical fact even though the frozen baseline explicitly excludes that worktree state.
findings.disposition: Removed the volatile one-change assertion. The document now states only the pinned Release default, records the zero-result pinned project-file grep, and keeps arming as a user-owned explicit-GO gate.

findings.issue: Baseline B1 is explicitly limited to two publisher modules, but the output stated a server-wide absence of periodic republishing without auditing callers.
findings.disposition: Preserved B1's scope and audited the external scheduler path. broadcast_rates_once wakes periodically, but topic publication is inside the payload-is_changed branch, so the supported conclusion is absence of an unconditional data-plane heartbeat or republish contract.

findings.issue: Several multi-claim units had a real citation that supported only the first clause, allowing the remaining operational assertion to borrow unrelated provenance.
findings.disposition: Added the missing pinned lines for Date()-based graph ingestion, current-rate/validRange flow, existing B1/B4 tests, post-ACK snapshot order, dormant AST tripwire, and the full auth_executor resource-bound warning.

findings.issue: The conservative claim lint omitted current-code assertions that lacked its exact cue/verb shape, so a green 55-entry ledger was not an exhaustive semantic review.
findings.disposition: Performed a broader reverse audit of every logical unit and all 86 output requirements, added local baseline or pinned file-line evidence, and regenerated the ledger at 59 explicitly reviewed candidates.

findings.issue: The cutover inventory said GraphViewModel had no consuming View and grouped its runtime object with zero-use symbols. RootView still consumes it for stop(), and the object installs callbacks and observers even though the legacy graph UI is not mounted.
findings.disposition: Separated zero-call symbols from the live GraphViewModel object and expanded the removal scope to callback, observer, environment, and stop wiring while preserving the no-production-start conclusion.

findings.issue: The first C2 draft kept an unconditional anonymous-subscribe statement and cited only the first line of each new stage layer. Those locators did not establish the enum/default, filter result, dispatcher registration, production injection, unsubscribe behavior, or pre-flag observation ordering.
findings.disposition: Rewrote the anonymous path as stage-dependent and cited complete pinned ranges for config, rollout policy, dispatcher application, production injection, unsubscribe, and metric ordering. The documents now distinguish the code default from the unmeasured operating stage and keep the premium/USDT gap open.

findings.issue: Moving pinned source lines and changing the anonymous-stage prose invalidated reviewed-unit hashes. Treating all drift as mechanical would have carried the obsolete unconditional-anonymous detail into the new claims.
findings.disposition: Carried forward only nine byte-identical classifications, reviewed the changed premium-gap and stage units independently, and regenerated an exact 60-entry ledger with 48 code facts and 12 normative units.

findings.issue: After Codex modified the final C2 documents and ledger, retaining a single 'independent semantic reviewer' attribution made Codex both co-author and global reviewer. The hashes were valid, but the independence claim was not.
findings.disposition: Replaced the global-independence claim with schema-v2 reciprocal cross-review. The journal records two non-self review edges, explicitly states that no participant is independent of the whole artifact, and the validator rejects self-review, one-way review, and false global-independence controls.

findings.issue: The first schema-v2 validator checked non-self review edges and exact duplicate prose, but did not bind participant authored/reviewed summaries to edge scopes. Reworded self-review or unrelated participant scopes therefore passed while the edges remained unchanged.
findings.disposition: Made review-edge scopes the canonical work units, required participant summaries to equal the scopes derived from their outgoing and incoming edges, rejected scope reuse across edges, and added adversarial controls for reworded self-review, participant/edge disagreement, and reused scopes. Scope labels and author/reviewer assignments remain explicitly attested rather than mechanically proven.

findings.issue: send_initial_snapshots built and sent payloads directly after subscription registration without rechecking the shared lease gate, even though leased_subscribers documents itself as the single gate shared by every publish path. A lease could expire, or the registry entry could disappear, while the snapshot builder ran in to_thread outside the authentication wire deadline, and the initial snapshot would still be sent. The defect escaped because the structural guards covered dispatcher publish functions but not the initial-snapshot module, and because the original unit tests invoked send_initial_snapshots with no registry state and therefore could not express lease eligibility at all.
findings.disposition: Commit 882d92b reuses leased_subscribers after each snapshot build and immediately before send_json. Leaseless E1 subscriptions still receive snapshots, only the ineligible topic is skipped, and five regression tests cover a valid lease, an expired lease, a leaseless subscription, registry disappearance during build, and skip-versus-abort. A naive registry.get_lease() check was rejected because its None conflates leaseless subscription with vanished registration. The reviewer inspected the implementation and call paths and independently ran the 33 direct unit tests; the author's three mutation controls were reviewed as reported but were not independently rerun by the reviewer.

findings.issue: The first S2a re-baseline attempt updated the baseline facts but left two current-code locators in the generated handoff document pointing at pre-882d92b line numbers. The author classified them as frozen archive quotations and declined to touch them; that classification was wrong. The archive line carries no locator at all, so both ranges are current-code claims owned by the generated document, and the claim ledger had copied one of them as a code_fact. Nothing in the hash chain detects this: every hash stayed internally consistent while the locators pointed at the wrong lines.
findings.disposition: Both ranges were remapped from the pre-commit file by content with function-scope disambiguation (275-296 to 277-307, 275-286 to 277-297) and the affected claim-ledger unit was regenerated from the validator's own candidate extractor rather than edited by hand. The reviewer identified one of the two stale ranges; the author found the second while remapping. Range existence is now mechanically checked for RID-contained backtick locators, every backtick locator in the baseline, and full-canonical-document Markdown #L links, but semantic entailment remains procedural.

findings.issue: The authenticated planner rejected a legal request shape. Its partition check compared the summed group sizes against the size of their union, so a request repeating the same topic raised ValueError in every stage even though the dispatcher and the wire preserve duplicate topics and request order.
findings.disposition: The check now forbids only pairwise intersection between partitions and verifies with a Counter that the partition preserves every input occurrence. Two regressions cover duplicates inside one group and duplicate occurrences across the plan.

findings.issue: A malformed policy value passed all three invariants and was approved as premium-only in the final stage. The invariants compared keys only, the derived entitlement set silently excluded the row because it was not the enum member, and the planner's broad else-branch classified it by stage. An entitlement-requiring product misconfigured this way would have been granted with premium alone.
findings.disposition: Policy values are validated where they are read and where the invariant runs, and the planner branches explicitly per enum member with a raising else. A regression injects an extended enum to prove the else-branch is load-bearing: a future member is rejected rather than silently classified.

findings.issue: The structural guard that keeps the policy table independent of the publisher constants inspected only top-level bindings. Rebinding inside a conditional, subscript assignment, and dict.update() all bypassed it, so the coverage equality could have become a tautology without any test noticing.
findings.disposition: The guard now rejects every rebinding form and duplicate literal keys, and the table is additionally frozen at runtime. Three counterexamples are permanent regressions.

findings.issue: Seven guards introduced by this slice had no discriminating test. Deleting the premium-only revocation, replacing the three-axis lease with the identity-only calculator, re-reading the clock for the premium-only lease, removing the plan boundary comparison, and removing either UID binding check each left the full suite green. The guards worked, but nothing would have caught their removal.
findings.disposition: Each guard gained a regression that observes the failure at the boundary rather than asserting the implementation. All seven mutations were re-run and now fail.

findings.issue: The shared entitlement guard is called at two REST decision boundaries, but only one was locked. The existing shortcut tests used a topic promoted to entitlement-gated, which fails the shortcut condition and therefore reaches the guard in the other function; removing the resolve-level call changed nothing. The uncovered path is a non-gated topic taking the shortcut while the table is malformed, where no guard runs at all.
findings.disposition: A regression exercises a non-gated topic against an expanded table. Removing the resolve-level guard now fails.

findings.issue: The C2 re-baseline moved citation locators onto the new commit while leaving the sentences that describe that code unchanged. Four places kept asserting that WS has no premium enforcement for FX/USDT, that the only per-user judgement is KRX, and that those topics enter a free_accepted list — while the same commit had implemented the enforcement path and renamed that variable away. The re-baseline procedure is content-anchored: it locates the same source line in the new file, which by construction cannot detect a prose claim that has become false while the code it cites still exists. Every gate passed — preflight compares paths, verify checks structure, and the hash chain proves only internal consistency — so the documents were re-sealed under a new SHA with inverted meaning.
findings.disposition: The affected passages now describe the three-stage implementation and code default without inferring the production stage or activation history. The exact-phrase tripwire was replaced by a planner-derived stage-matrix comparison plus targeted stale-claim controls. SEM-019 records the completed reciprocal cross-review of that correction.

findings.issue: The C3 correction did not close SEM-018. It left contradictory pre-S2c prose beside the new stage table, split the baseline C2 continuation under unrelated C4/C5 bullets, retained stale claim-ledger details and incomplete code ranges, and promoted the code default into unmeasured production-state and activation-history assertions. Its exact-phrase tripwire accepted equivalent stale wording, while the semantic journal kept verdict=pass without a review edge covering C3. During the correction, the baseline-reference parser also misread the e474 fragment of commit 0cfe474 as a baseline ID whenever the same logical unit mentioned baseline evidence.
findings.disposition: Codex rewrote the affected requirements, corrected the pinned ranges, regenerated the six changed claim-ledger entries from the canonical candidate/provenance extractors, strengthened the tripwire with a planner-derived stage matrix and explicit no-inference controls, and added identifier boundaries plus a commit-hash counterexample to the baseline-reference parser. Claude then independently reproduced the measurement conflation and baseline-ID defect, verified that reverting the regex fix fails, and mutation-tested the matrix in three directions: a false documented cell, a code policy change with the table untouched, and a new stage without a table row. The reciprocal review edges record both scopes.

findings.issue: The C4 closure left lifecycle text internally contradictory: fixed findings still said that SEM-019 was open, unreviewed, and required needs_cross_review while the top-level verdict was pass. The stage-matrix gate also represented the aggregate columns with only fx:usd-krw and did not inspect USDT's authenticated partition; runtime mutations that changed only JPY, EUR, or USDT all survived the document-table comparison.
findings.disposition: Codex rewrote the closed-finding dispositions in completed-review tense and derived the aggregate columns from the canonical publisher constants: every anonymous FX member is compared, the identified column requires one uniform authorization class across all FX topics plus USDT, and a permanent counterexample changes each aggregate member independently. Cross-review confirmed both halves against the closing commit rather than accepting them. The lifecycle contradiction was reproduced at 79d93f2 (SEM-018 and SEM-019 carried fixed status while their prose still said the review was pending and the verdict was pass). The representation gap was reproduced too: at that commit a policy change confined to fx:jpy-krw, fx:eur-krw, or usdt:krw left the documented matrix equal to the derived one, so the earlier report that the gate discriminated in three directions was over-general — all three mutations used had moved the USD cell. Against the corrected gate the same four single-topic mutations each fail, and the regression exercises them without editing any file.

findings.issue: C5 marked SEM-020 fixed and restored verdict=pass, but its first residual limit still said that the SEM-020 follow-up was not covered by a pass verdict until the opposite participant reviewed it. The pass review edge also claimed the C5 cross-review before Codex had reviewed that closing state. Separately, the journal still said the current operating values were unmeasured while the C5 commit message reported a point-in-time observation; that observation is outside the journal's hash-bound evidence. The same commit inferred that nonzero counters were not synthetic merely because they had been zero immediately after restart, although these counters carry no traffic-provenance dimension.
findings.disposition: Codex removed the unreviewed C5 scope from the pass edge, rewrote the stale residual limit, and taught the validator to reject pending-review language in fixed dispositions and residual limits, using a synthetic closed journal as the positive control. Cross-review reproduced both halves: at 5f9aa74 the first residual limit still said the SEM-020 follow-up was not covered by a pass verdict, while the verdict was pass and SEM-020 was fixed. The closing self-check that reported no pending language had swept findings only and not residual limits, so a complete-sounding claim came from a partial scan — the third instance of that shape in this session. Both validator additions are load-bearing: replacing the synthetic closed fixture with the live open journal, or emptying the pending-language patterns, each turns the counterexample suite red. The Codex-authored technical work is recorded in the OpenAI Codex → Claude Code edge; SEM-022 corrects the separate closure protocol.

findings.issue: C6 generalized a workflow mistake into an impossibility claim: it said closing the journal cannot be cross-reviewed and therefore made the closing bookkeeping self-attested. A terminating protocol exists — the author prepares the complete fixed/pass candidate first, the opposite participant reviews that exact tree without editing it, and the unchanged tree is committed. The commit operation does not create new file content; any post-review tree edit invalidates the attestation and reopens review. C6 also said review edges record technical work only but omitted the Codex-authored SEM-021 validator and residual corrections that Claude had just reviewed. Finally, nonzero provenance-free counters establish observed request events, not nonzero organic or end-user transition impact.
findings.disposition: Codex replaced the self-attestation exception with a terminating closure protocol, added the missing SEM-021 technical scope to the review edges, and taught the validator to reject the self-attestation wording in a pass journal. Cross-review accepted the correction rather than defending the earlier claim: the regress was an artifact of this process, not a property of review. Each round the reviewer kept editing after reviewing, which manufactured new unreviewed content; if the author prepares the complete candidate and the opposite participant reviews that exact tree without touching it, the commit contains only reviewed content and the edge asserting that review is verifiable by the reviewer itself, so nothing is circular. One verification held as written and one did not. Emptying the pass-lifecycle patterns turns the suite red. Replacing the closed fixture with the live journal was red only while that journal was open: in the final pass tree the helper became a no-op and the mutation survived, so the load-bearing claim had been checked in one state and asserted about another. The counterexample base now starts from a synthetic open journal, which makes the helper load-bearing regardless of the live verdict. The omission was reproduced too — at 624e431 both edges still ended at C4-era scopes while the closing commit message said the recorded scopes were now technical work only. Reviewing that correction in turn found the scaffold unlocked: turning _synthetic_open_journal into a no-op restores the original defect silently, because the base falls back to the live journal and the closed fixture goes inert again. A regression now asserts that the synthetic open state really produces errors, so all three mutations — the fixture, the pending-language patterns, and the scaffold itself — are red in the final pass tree.

findings.issue: The token-bearing C2 candidate mechanically remapped the legacy /api/graph/{currency} citation from main.py:1862 to main.py:1874 because the same unrelated KRX reconciliation comment moved there; the actual route is at main.py:2416. Exact-tree review initially accepted textual continuity without checking whether the target entailed the surrounding claim, reproducing the SEM-018 failure mode. The same candidate called the historical S2c value 56 and the current value 51 comparable locator-occurrence counts even though they came from different procedures, and described the remaining guard as path-only without stating that the citation existence test sees only backtick-form locators inside manifest-owned RID blocks. Markdown-link locators and prose outside those blocks are invisible to that test.
findings.disposition: The in-scope legacy graph link now points to main.py:2416 in both its label and #L anchor. The residual limits remove the cross-slice numeric comparison, define this C2's reproducible procedural inventory as 27 changed locator occurrences in five source documents plus 24 changed occurrences in the derived claim ledger, and state the citation gate's exact syntax, RID, existence, and entailment boundaries. At SEM-023 closure, three pre-existing broken Markdown-link locators outside ADR-041's hash-bound section remained separate debt; SEM-024 later repaired them and added a separate full-document Markdown-link existence gate.

findings.issue: SEM-023 deliberately left three pre-existing Markdown locator debts outside ADR-041: two in-bounds links pointed at unrelated current code and one target exceeded its pinned file. The existing FILE_LINE test scanned only backtick-form locators in manifest-owned RID blocks, so all three were invisible. The initial inventory also counted only labels beginning with app/, while the same canonical document uses shorthand labels such as crud.py; a complete structural scan must key on the link target's #L anchor rather than the label prefix. The baseline is not a manifest-owned RID document either, so its 40 backtick locators were hash-bound but received no pinned path or bounds check.
findings.disposition: Historical ADR-026 and ADR-031 facts now link to exact 40-character commit blobs where the quoted code existed, while ADR-030's current per-key freshness link points to the pinned executing range. Two sibling prose locators in ADR-031 were converted to the same immutable historical model instead of being remapped onto unrelated current code. A separate gate scans the full text of all six canonical documents, validates local #L links at the lock pin and same-repository historical links at their explicit commit, checks bounds and label/anchor line agreement, and rejects mutable short-SHA history. Another full-file gate validates all 40 baseline backtick locators at the pinned server or iOS commit and fails if extraction becomes empty. Synthetic counterexamples lock zero, inverted and out-of-range bounds, label drift, mutable history, and the pre-ADR-041 scan surface. A targeted regression pins the manually reviewed ADR-030/031 targets; semantic entailment in general remains outside mechanical proof.

findings.issue: The first post-SEM-024 hardening pinned the baseline total and server/iOS split, but FILE_LINE still enumerated filename extensions. Removing md left every test green even though two canonical backtick locators use .md, and the RID surface also carries .conf alongside Python and Swift. A nonempty or repository-level inventory cannot prove that every extension-shaped locator remains visible.
findings.disposition: FILE_LINE now recognizes path-and-extension structure without enumerating extensions. An independently expressed, broader locator-shape oracle must produce the identical ordered extraction across the full baseline and all manifest-owned RID blocks, and a synthetic future extension is a positive control. The baseline additionally pins 40 total references split as server 30 and iOS 10. Removing the former md axis or restoring an extension allowlist now fails the targeted test.

findings.issue: The semantic-review counterexample suite generally asserted only that review_errors returned a nonempty list. Its self-review control produced four errors at once, so neutralizing the dedicated 'is self-review' branch still left three unrelated errors and the full suite stayed green. The protocol's core no-self-review rule therefore existed in production validation but its own branch was not load-bearing in the regression suite.
findings.disposition: The self-review control now requires the dedicated self-review diagnostic rather than accepting any error. A mutation that filters only that diagnostic fails while the unmodified positive control remains green. An exhaustive one-branch-at-a-time audit on 2026-08-13 neutralized each of the 40 errors.append sites with no invalid mutations: 32 still survived the suite and 8 were caught, including the self-review branch fixed here. The remaining 32 are explicitly bounded below as separate hardening work.

findings.issue: The a562391 commit message inferred that zero topic subscribes during a 46-connection window meant no topic-v2 client was deployed. The deployed cfc8659 dispatcher observed only anonymous subscribes; token-bearing messages were structurally invisible because the later elif branch did not exist. The same 46-connection point was read live over SSH but no preserved snapshot covers that later interval. Commit messages, tags, deployment reports, and agent memory are not among this journal's hash-bound inputs merely because they describe the reviewed code.
findings.disposition: The immutable 9f0aec9 commit message supersedes the inference: that window establishes zero observed anonymous subscribes only, not absence of token-bearing clients. The unpreserved 46-connection reading is not activation evidence. This journal records the correction and makes the attestation boundary explicit; unverified token-bearing candidate requests become observable only after deploying the landed pre-flag metric, and production activation still requires preserved direct measurements plus the separate RevenueCat canary decision.

findings.issue: Four coverage-surface controls could shrink while their own tests stayed green. The docs-workflow AST candidate helper could return an empty set, because the test asserted only candidate-minus-workflow emptiness. The semantic-drift loader silently skipped missing paths and accepted at least eight texts although its declared surface has nine. The RID citation checks had no reference inventory, so removing a cited RID block from their extracted surface left the remaining references sufficient. MARKDOWN_LINK_DOCS was both the parametrization source and the only document list, so removing a canonical document that currently has zero #L links simply removed its test case. These are validation-surface gaps rather than current locator or production-code defects.
findings.disposition: The docs-workflow tripwire now pins the seven currently discovered Markdown-literal modules before comparing them with the workflow. Semantic drift fails closed on every declared path and locks seven documents plus two ledgers as nine unique ordered inputs. RID backtick validation pins 125 references by all six destinations and by server 61 versus iOS 64. The Markdown-link gate independently pins the six canonical documents, including five that currently have zero links. Empty discovery, one missing semantic input, one dropped cited RID block, and one removed zero-link document now each fail; intentional surface changes require an explicit reviewed inventory update.

findings.issue: SEM-026 closed only the no-self-review branch. An exhaustive one-branch-at-a-time audit measured 32 of the 40 errors.append sites as still neutralisable with the suite green, because the remaining counterexamples asserted only that review_errors returned a non-empty list and adjacent diagnostics satisfied that assertion.
findings.disposition: A table of 32 controls now mutates the closed fixture and asserts the specific diagnostic each branch emits, so neutralising any single append site fails a named control. Controls are not required to trigger their branch in isolation; asserting the target diagnostic is sufficient and keeps the table small. Re-running the audit on this tree reports 40 sites, 0 invalid mutations, 40 red and 0 survivors. The claim is bounded to append-site coverage: one site inside a loop emits for many participant fields, scope flags and finding keys, so 40 of 40 does not mean every variant of every rule is locked.

findings.issue: The C1 review round for the RevenueCat provider slice (7c8a890) shipped three evidence claims that did not reproduce: a mutation-attribution claim (a 201-only Determined(False) injection was reported to survive the pre-hardening scenario table, but the existing '201 created active' row already killed it — the experiment had never been run), a logging claim (the dedicated 404 test was described as locking the common error log including status, but it only matched the formatted message, which never carries extra fields), and a gate report (preflight was reported as E_CODECHANGED although the actual gate run printed no such line). All three were caught by the reviewer re-running the experiments instead of reading the claims.
findings.disposition: The mutation battery now uses a 201-only truthiness parser as the discriminating mutation, reproduced on both tables before adoption (survives the old two-row table, dies on the new '201 expired' row); the 404 test asserts record.status == 404 from logs.records; gate reports quote rc values printed by the same run. Same lineage as SEM-018/SEM-023: verifying a mechanical property (suite green, plausible claim text) is not verifying the semantic property (the experiment actually discriminates, the log actually carries the field). Bounded claim: the 201 rows are representative of the 200 hardening matrix, not a full differential oracle — the shared-branch property itself is locked by the 201-to-200-only mutation.

findings.issue: The C2 R-GATE-1 ledger note closed with 'WS classification unchanged (ProtocolViolation -> persistent unavailable)'. That conflates two properties: the classify_premium mapping table (untouched by C1) and the end-to-end WS verdict for a 404 response, which C1 intentionally changed — pre-C1 a 404 produced Determined(False) and therefore Denied('premium_required'); post-C1 it produces ProtocolViolation and therefore Unavailable(PERSISTENT). The false sentence passed the C2 exact-tree review and its pass edge; it was caught by the opposite participant reading the mapped path end-to-end, not by any gate — no gate binds ledger note prose to code behaviour.
findings.disposition: The note now states both halves separately: the ProtocolViolation mapping is unchanged, and the 404 WS outcome changed by design from Denied(premium_required) to Unavailable(PERSISTENT) because the 404->Determined(False) inflow was removed. Provider and authorization code are untouched by this correction. Reopened per the closure rule with a new opposite-participant work unit and edge (C3). Mapping-function invariance is not verdict invariance when an input's type assignment moves — same family as SEM-018/SEM-023/SEM-030: a mechanical property (the mapping table diff is empty) was reported as the semantic property (behaviour unchanged).

findings.issue: R-LOAD-3's evidence E2 cited app/topic_initial_snapshot.py:305 for the claim that initial snapshots are built sequentially per connection, quoting both the loop and the to_thread call. Line 305 carries neither. The loop is at 310 and the to_thread build at 316. spec/topic-only-baseline-facts.md E2 quoted the same two elements but cited only :316, so both documents were partially wrong and in different ways — and an earlier draft of this correction claimed the baseline was already right, which the reviewer refuted by reading it. The citation gates did not object to either because they check path existence and in-bounds only, which restates the SEM-012/SEM-023/SEM-024 residual. Both drifts surfaced from reading during a reconnect-storm implementation audit, not from any gate.
findings.disposition: Both E2 locators now cite 310-316, the range that contains both quoted elements. No code changed and no pinned commit moved, but the baseline file itself changed, so the chain advances: baseline hash in the lock, manifest baseline_sha, the baseline and manifest SHA lines in all six output documents, and the derived ledger and journal hashes. The E2 bullets are not extracted claim candidates, so no ledger unit text changed (candidate set equals ledger key set, checked before and after). Bounded: this fixes two locators found by reading and does not establish that other backtick locators entail their surrounding claims.

findings.issue: The re-baseline for S0 was scoped from a reviewer-supplied list of moved app/main.py locators. An exhaustive scan was claimed but the pattern assumed how the path is written, so the count recorded here was wrong: counted as citation occurrence sites, twelve source-document sites were affected (DECISIONS 2, baseline 3, CLIENT 2, HAND 1, GRAPH 2, FREE_TIER 1, USDT_TOPIC 1), not ten. The list this commit worked from had omitted DECISIONS' legacy graph markdown link and both GRAPH links, and the scan itself never saw the FREE_TIER and USDT_TOPIC citations at all because they use the abbreviated main.py:NNNN form. Every site the scan did see was then checked against the file rather than moved by arithmetic, and the two GRAPH links turned out not to point at what their prose claimed even at the current pin, so a mechanical +18 would have carried the error forward at a new pin. That is the SEM-023 failure repeated: verifying that a line moved is not verifying that the target supports the claim. SEM-034 records the scan-completeness failure and corrects these counts.
findings.disposition: Eight occurrence sites were remapped after reading each new target: the legacy graph route decorator (2434), the v2 snapshot route (3053), verify_firebase_token (3088), require_premium (3091) and the invalid_token branch (3168-3175) — five unique targets. Two GRAPH_API_V2_CONTRACT.md links were found to be pre-existing debt and deliberately left in place by this commit with their true targets recorded; two further wrong citations in FREE_TIER_ACCESS_MODEL_PLAN.md and USDT_TOPIC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md were not found at all here. So this commit left four wrong citations standing, and the next commit corrected all four (SEM-034). Counts in this record are stated in occurrence sites; the derived claim-ledger carries the same strings and was regenerated. Bounded: the scan covered app/main.py citations only.

findings.issue: SEM-033 claimed an exhaustive scan of app/main.py citations, and the claim was wrong twice for the same reason: the search pattern encoded an assumption about how the path is written. The first pattern required the literal prefix app/main.py:, so the abbreviated form main.py:NNNN was invisible — that hid FREE_TIER_ACCESS_MODEL_PLAN.md's topic_unavailable citation and USDT_TOPIC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md's source-notification-settings citation, both of which point past the insertion point. A second pattern excluded a slash before app/, so the exchange-rate/app/main.py: form used by the baseline was also missed. The true count of affected occurrence sites is twelve, not ten, and the pre-existing debt is four citations, not two. A reviewer found the first gap; the second was found by rescanning with a directory-prefix-independent pattern.
findings.disposition: All four pre-existing wrong citations were corrected after reading their targets rather than shifting them: GRAPH_API_V2_CONTRACT.md's legacy graph route 1831 to 2434 and its period cache 2024-2046 to 2627-2670 plus 2717-2719 (the first correction cited only the read path and was completed in SEM-035), FREE_TIER_ACCESS_MODEL_PLAN.md's topic_unavailable 2771 to 3120-3123, the range that also carries the flag-off meaning the prose asserts, and USDT_TOPIC_MIGRATION_PLAN.md's source-notification-settings 2226 to the four decorator ranges 3761-3764, 3843-3846, 3874-3877 and 3966-3969, because the prose claims four methods and a single open-ended start line proves only the first. SEM-033's counts were corrected in place to twelve sites and four debts. The methodological lesson is recorded as the finding itself: a citation scan must not encode how the path is spelled, because every prefix assumption silently shrinks the net, and the word exhaustive should not be used unless the pattern is directory-prefix-independent — it still assumes the main.py:NNNN locator form. None of the three source documents holding those four citations is inside the six gated documents, so the current locator and citation gates observed none of the four.

findings.issue: The SEM-034 corrections were themselves incomplete in three ways. The period-cache citation covered declaration, read and eviction but not the store at app/main.py:2718, so it did not finish proving the prose claim that an in-memory cache is used. The four source-notification-settings ranges were written with three abbreviated :NNNN continuations, which the directory-prefix-independent scanner that SEM-034 prescribes cannot find — the lesson was violated inside the commit that recorded it. And the non-hash-bound C3 commit message reported the old-pin evidence with the two values swapped: at 2635674^ line 2226 is a docstring quote and line 2771 is blank, not the other way round. Commit messages are outside the journal's hash-bound inputs, so the correction lives here rather than in the message.
findings.disposition: The period cache now cites 2627-2670 for declaration/read/eviction and 2717-2719 for the store. All four method ranges are written self-contained as app/main.py:NNNN-NNNN so the scanner finds each one independently. The swapped old-pin values are corrected here; the conclusion they supported — that both citations were already wrong before S0 — is unchanged, since neither line carried the cited content. Bounded: this closes the citations touched by SEM-033/034 and does not re-audit citations to other files.

findings.issue: The first S3 C2 re-derivation carried locators computed against a pre-edit tree — a one-line docstring change landed after the mapping run shifted every line below it, so five remapped ranges were short by one line or ended before the statements their prose asserts, and the D6 candidate pointed at a comment line (a new off-by-one introduced by that stale mapping, not a pre-existing state). The measurement also surfaced two pre-existing under-specified single-point locators that predate S3: D3 cited only the warning line while its prose asserts isolation plus the None skip, and D6 cited only the membership-check line while its prose asserts the per-topic skip, which lived on a later line. The reviewer detected all of this by reading the actual trees — old pin and new — while the citation gates cannot, since they check path existence and in-bounds only (the SEM-012/023/024 residual).
findings.disposition: Ranges re-derived against the committed C1 tree: D3 now cites :337-346 covering the isolation except and the None skip, D6 cites :359-366 covering the pre-send gate and its skip, R-HAND-4 :298-335 and E2 :319-335 cover the full to_thread call, and the R-HAND-1 isolation range :298-346 reaches the skip statement. Classification: three content-identical moves, five widened semantically re-verified ranges. Bounded: closes the S3-touched locators only; the lesson — re-derive locators only after the final tree is fixed — joins the recurring-mistake list.

residual_limits: Natural-language completeness and citation entailment are not mechanically provable. This pass covers only the work units explicitly listed in review_process.review_edges; later changes must reopen the verdict and obtain a new opposite-participant review edge. The boundary is the edge list itself, not a finding number, because a hand-written endpoint goes stale on the next round.
Negative repository facts use full-tree searches at the pinned commits and must be rerun if either pinned commit changes.
The documents remain Draft implementation contracts. This pass confirms the cited C1 code path at the pinned commit, not operating activation or completion of R-GATE-1.

This hash-bound semantic review does not establish mutable production state. Commit 5f9aa74 reports a separate read-only observation at 2026-08-12 13:09 UTC, but its raw command, host/container identity, and output are not preserved in the reviewed inputs; activation still requires a fresh direct measurement.
The 2026-08-12 historical amendment before ADR-041 is outside the document hash used by this journal and remains a separately reviewed, non-hash-bound note.
Release arming remains excluded from the frozen baseline and requires a separate explicit GO.
The initial-snapshot lease gate authorizes the start of send_json, not its completion; an in-flight send may finish after the lease expires.
A post-ACK snapshot skip is fail-closed but produces no removal, reauthorization, or close notification, so a client can be told a topic was accepted and then receive no initial data.

The shared lease gate performs an O(number of subscribers) scan and set allocation per topic. This is accepted for the current scale and supported-topic bound, not established as a large-scale guarantee.

Citation existence has two syntax gates: backtick-form `path:N[-M]` locators inside manifest-owned RID blocks plus the full baseline are checked at the lock pin, and Markdown `#L` links across the full text of the six canonical documents are checked at the lock pin or an explicit same-repository 40-character commit. Both gates check only path existence, bounds, and limited label/anchor agreement; neither proves that the target entails the surrounding prose. Backtick locators in non-RID prose outside the baseline, unlinked prose line numbers, and semantic drift can still survive a green re-baseline (SEM-012/SEM-023/SEM-024).

In the final stage, every authenticated subscribe containing at least one authorizable topic makes one cache-free RevenueCat HTTP round trip: the WS authorization path calls fetch_revenuecat_result directly and the stale-cache fallback exists only in the REST helper. This availability and latency coupling is unmitigated and gates activation.
FX enforcement is bounded by the unauthenticated legacy broadcast until Stage B. This slice closes the topic contract, not the service-wide paywall (R-OPEN-4).
The working tree was edited concurrently by two agents during this review. The reported verification is pinned to one tree hash rather than a continuous observation of a frozen tree.

This token-bearing C2's procedural drift inventory found 27 changed locator occurrences in five source documents and 24 changed occurrences in the derived claim ledger, for 51 total. This count excludes unchanged citations and is not comparable to historical C2 counts unless the same extractor, base, and scope are rerun. RID-contained backtick locators and full-document Markdown links now receive mechanical existence and bounds checks, but correctness of moved claims still rests on exact-tree semantic review.

Re-baselining verifies that citations point at existing code, not that the surrounding prose is still true. SEM-018 shows the two can diverge while every gate passes; only reading each cited passage against the new behaviour closes it, and that step is procedural.

The forbidden-phrase check that keeps the code default from being promoted to an operational fact has no exemption for a measured statement: once production is actually sampled, the same forbidden substring still trips even if source and timestamp are appended. A measured result must use distinct wording such as '2026-08-12 direct measurement found WS_TOPIC_AUTH_STAGE=compatibility' and include its source and timestamp. This is a deliberate cost of phrase matching; adding semantic exemptions would make the check itself a guess.

The stage matrix binds the documented aggregate columns to the planners, but its subject is the R-INV-2 table alone. Prose elsewhere in the same documents can still contradict the code without any gate noticing; SEM-018 was found by reading, not by a check.

The anonymous rollout counters contain request and connection-event counts but no traffic-provenance label. A zero immediately after restart establishes the observation interval only; it cannot prove that later events were organic rather than manual or synthetic probes. Nonzero counters therefore establish matching request events, not nonzero organic traffic or end-user transition impact.

Journal closure terminates when the author prepares the complete fixed/pass candidate first and the opposite participant reviews that exact tree without modifying it. Committing the unchanged tree adds no unreviewed file content; any post-review tree edit invalidates the attestation and requires another review. globally_independent_reviewer=false limits independence of the artifact as a whole, but does not make reciprocal review of an exact final tree impossible.

The unverified_token_bearing counters run before Firebase verification and store fixed-cardinality request and connection-event counts only. They do not establish valid-token demand, authenticated users, or actual RevenueCat calls. final_stage_rc_candidate is conditional on the injected topic-availability snapshot and later dispatcher, stage, and token gates; process restart resets every counter.

SEM-024 repairs the three known Markdown-link locator debts outside ADR-041, adds a full-canonical-document #L gate, and validates all baseline backtick locators against the pins. SEM-025 removes the backtick extractor's extension allowlist and checks it against an independently expressed locator-shape oracle. Those checks cannot discover plain prose line numbers without a recognized locator and cannot prove semantic entailment; historical code claims therefore use immutable full-SHA blobs, while target meaning still requires review.

The one-branch-at-a-time audit that measured 32 of 40 errors.append sites as neutralisable (33 before SEM-026) is closed by SEM-029: every site now fails a control that names its own diagnostic, re-measured on this tree as 40 sites, 0 invalid, 40 red, 0 survivors. Coverage is of append sites, not of rule variants — a single site inside a loop serves many participant fields, scope flags and finding keys, and those variants remain unaudited.

Commit messages, annotated tags, deployment reports, terminal transcripts, and agent memory are outside this journal's hash-bound inputs unless a review edge explicitly identifies and preserves the exact artifact. In particular, a562391's unpreserved 46-connection observation is not promoted to activation evidence; 9f0aec9 corrects only its invalid client-absence inference.

SEM-028 pins the currently reviewed extraction surfaces: seven Markdown-literal test modules, nine semantic-drift inputs, 125 RID backtick locators, and six canonical Markdown-link documents. These inventories prevent silent shrinkage but do not prove that heuristic discovery is complete, that dynamically assembled paths are visible, or that a locator semantically entails its prose; legitimate additions and removals require reviewing and updating the corresponding inventory.
